messages:
From: security@argenta.com (Helen O'Neil) <security@argenta.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observed anomalous activity — request for IR plan & contact

Hi Sofia,

Argenta's security operations detected a spike of anomalous API calls originating from one of your serving clusters that correlated with two elevated transactions on our side on 2027-06-09 22:14 UTC. We're still triaging but want to notify you and request your incident response plan, on-call liaison, and any initial telemetry you can share.

To be specific, could you provide:
- Your IR lead contact for this issue (phone + email)
- The IR plan/communication matrix you follow for customer-impacting events (redacted where needed)
- Any sanitized post-incident summary and telemetry extracts once available

We'd like to set a 30m call this week to align on containment and evidence exchange. Please let me know availability.

Thanks,
Helen O'Neil
Senior Security Manager — Argenta Bank
security@argenta.com

Helen,

Thanks for the heads-up and for sending the alert file. We're taking this seriously. I will be the primary liaison for Redwood on this matter. Immediate next steps from our side:

1) I've opened an internal incident (IR-427) and assigned an incident lead.
2) We'll provide a redacted copy of our Incident Response Plan and a sanitized post-incident summary within 72 hours.
3) We'll export the requested telemetry (rate-limited) and share a secure Drive folder and an encrypted archive.

Proposed call windows (PST): 2027-06-11 09:00–11:00, 2027-06-11 14:00–16:00. If those don't work, tell me preferred times.

For transparency, could you confirm the list of Argenta IPs and the two transaction IDs you referenced so we can scope logs precisely?

Subject: RE: Argenta security notification — request for IR liaison and sanitized summary

Helen / Miguel,

Follow-up from Redwood: please find our sanitized summary and artifact index attached. Key points:

- Summary: On 2027-06-09 we observed an unusual request pattern that matched Argenta's report. The root cause was an ephemeral misconfiguration in a routing rule that allowed a narrow window of increased retries from a subset of client keys. No customer data was exfiltrated; the elevated transactions were triggered by duplicate submission attempts.

- Actions taken: we rolled a configuration fix (2027-06-10 02:16 UTC), invalidated the impacted ephemeral keys, and ran a scoped reingestion to correct duplicates.

- Artifacts provided: redwood_ir_plan_v2.pdf (redacted plan), sanitized-postmortem-argenta-20270615.pdf (post-incident summary), telemetry_extracts_20270614.zip (redacted logs). We've placed the artifacts in the secure Drive folder linked below and provided an encrypted zip for your ingestion.

Links and verification: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_argenta_ir_artifacts (access granted to Argenta security group). For chain-of-custody verification we've added a short audit record in IR-427: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/IR-427.

If Argenta wants a tight walkthrough, Marissa and Karthik are available tomorrow (2027-06-17) for a 30m technical walk; Laura can join for comms. Proposed time: 09:30 PST.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Security & Privacy Manager
Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-2198
